mechanism_narrative: A low and declining unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which positively impacts consumer confidence and spending, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE is below 4%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate investment, which negatively impacts S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) is increasing, it signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 30% of instances when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS is increasing, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) during an economic expansion signals strong consumer demand and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST is increasing during an expansion, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) combined with an increase in real sales (RSAFS) signals strong economic activity and supply chain health, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 30% of instances when both INDPRO and RSAFS are increasing, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals inflationary pressures, leading to potential monetary policy tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals strong economic growth, leading to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 is increasing, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, if the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) also increases, it signals economic slowdown and tighter financial conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when both UNRATE and FEDFUNDS are increasing during a tightening cycle, the hypothesis is rejected.
